lead: Any two of the four two-port variables can be chosen to drive the other two. Hybrid parameters choose the input current I1 and the output voltage V2 as drivers, and produce the input voltage V1 and the output current I2. One driver is a current, the other is a voltage, so the set is called hybrid. The four constants carry mixed units: one ohm, one siemens, two plain ratios. That mix matches a transistor exactly, where the base is current-driven and the collector is voltage-loaded. The inverse hybrid (g) set turns the same two equations inside out, driving I1 and V2 from V1 and I2.
prereq: You need: 6.1 for the four port variables and their assumed current directions, 6.2 for the matrix view of a two-port, and dependent sources from Unit 1.

blocks.text: A two-port is seen only through two terminal pairs, so it has four external variables: V1, I1 at port 1 and V2, I2 at port 2. Z parameters drive the port with I1 and I2; Y parameters drive it with V1 and V2. Neither fits an amplifier, whose input is fed by a current and whose output is loaded by a voltage. The hybrid set drives with I1 and V2.
V₁ = h₁₁ I₁ + h₁₂ V₂        I₂ = h₂₁ I₁ + h₂₂ V₂
blocks.where: V₁, I₁ are the port-1 voltage and current; V₂, I₂ are the port-2 voltage and current, with I₂ taken as entering port 2; h₁₁ is the short-circuit input impedance in Ω; h₁₂ is the open-circuit reverse voltage gain, dimensionless; h₂₁ is the short-circuit forward current gain, dimensionless; h₂₂ is the open-circuit output admittance in S.

blocks.text: The two equations do different jobs. The first builds the input voltage from a drop (h11 I1) and a feed-through from the output (h12 V2). The second builds the output current from a controlled source (h21 I1) and a local admittance (h22 V2). Stacked as matrices, [V₁; I₂] = [h] × [I₁; V₂], where [h] is the 2×2 hybrid matrix.
Because I2 is taken as entering port 2, a passive load is written V2 = −I2 Z_L. Keep that sign; it decides whether h21 comes out positive or negative in a test.
Each parameter is a ratio taken with one driver set to zero. V2 = 0 means shorting the output port with a wire. I1 = 0 means leaving the input port open. Two tests, four numbers.

The subscripts follow one rule: the first index is the port where you measure, the second is the port you excite. So h₁₂ reads "volts at port 1 per volt at port 2" with port 1 open. Read the table that way and you never have to memorise it.

In transistor work the same four numbers get different names: h₂₁ is the forward current gain β, written h_fe; h₁₁ is the input impedance h_ie; h₁₂ is the reverse voltage gain h_re, usually around 10⁻⁴; h₂₂ is the output admittance h_oe. All four are small-signal values measured at a stated bias point.
Solve the same two equations for I1 and V2 instead, and you get the inverse hybrid set.
I₁ = g₁₁ V₁ + g₁₂ I₂        V₂ = g₂₁ V₁ + g₂₂ I₂
blocks.where: g₁₁ is the open-circuit input admittance in S (measure with I₂ = 0); g₁₂ is the short-circuit reverse current gain, dimensionless (V₁ = 0); g₂₁ is the open-circuit forward voltage gain, dimensionless (I₂ = 0); g₂₂ is the short-circuit output impedance in Ω (V₁ = 0).

blocks.text: The two matrices are inverses of each other: [h] = [g]⁻¹.
h₁₁ = g₂₂ / Δ_g,  h₁₂ = −g₁₂ / Δ_g,  h₂₁ = −g₂₁ / Δ_g,  h₂₂ = g₁₁ / Δ_g
blocks.where: Δ_g = g₁₁ g₂₂ − g₁₂ g₂₁ is the determinant of the g matrix; the minus signs appear on both transfer terms. Full conversion algebra is in 6.5.

blocks.text: Watch the units across the swap: h₂₂ is an admittance in siemens while g₂₂ is an impedance in ohms. They are not reciprocals of each other. Only the whole matrices are inverses. Some syllabi call h the hybrid parameters and g the inverse hybrid parameters; only a few courses go past reading the two matrices off a datasheet.

figure.caption: The upper path builds V1 from I1 through h11 and from V2 through h12; the lower path builds I2 from I1 through h21 and from V2 through h22. The numbers are the worked example below, where the two terms of V1 cancel.

spec.title: h-parameter two-port
spec.aria: I1 and V2 drive the two h-parameter equations; the upper path builds V1, the lower path builds I2.

examples.question: A transistor at its bias point has h11 = 1 kΩ, h12 = 0.002, h21 = 50 and h22 = 20 μS. The input current is I1 = 10 μA and the output port is held at V2 = −5 V. Find the input voltage V1 and the output current I2.
steps: Write the hybrid equations: V1 = h11 I1 + h12 V2 and I2 = h21 I1 + h22 V2.
Convert to base units: h11 = 1000 Ω, h22 = 20 × 10⁻⁶ S, I1 = 10 × 10⁻⁶ A, V2 = −5 V.
Input drop term: h11 I1 = 1000 × 10 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.01 V.
Reverse feed-through term: h12 V2 = 0.002 × (−5) = −0.01 V.
Controlled source term: h21 I1 = 50 × 10 × 10⁻⁶ = 5 × 10⁻⁴ A = 0.5 mA.
Output admittance term: h22 V2 = 20 × 10⁻⁶ × (−5) = −1 × 10⁻⁴ A = −0.1 mA.
examples.answer: V1 = 0 V and I2 = 0.4 mA (4 × 10⁻⁴ A); at port 1 the forward drop and the reverse feed-through cancel exactly.

traps: h11 is measured with the output shorted (V2 = 0), not open. Opening the output changes the number completely; the short is what makes h11 a pure input impedance.
Unit slip: h11 is in ohms and h22 is in siemens, while h12 and h21 are plain ratios. Writing h11 in siemens, h22 in ohms, or h12 in volts costs marks.
Do not throw away the h12 V2 term as negligible unless the question says so. With V2 negative it can cancel the h11 I1 term exactly, and the cancellation is often the point of the sum.
g22 is an impedance while h22 is an admittance. They are not reciprocals; only the full matrices are inverses, and the transfer terms pick up minus signs.
The short-circuit output test gives h11 and h21 only. h12 and h22 need the input left open, so a single test cannot give all four.

quiz.q: Which two variables are the independent drivers in the h-parameter set?
quiz.a: The input current I1 and the output voltage V2. The set produces V1 and I2.

quiz.q: State the unit of each of the four h parameters.
quiz.a: h11 in ohms, h12 dimensionless, h21 dimensionless, h22 in siemens.

quiz.q: Why is this set called hybrid, and why is it the natural choice for a transistor?
quiz.a: The drivers are one current and one voltage, so the constants carry mixed units: that is the hybrid nature. A transistor input is fed by a current and its output is terminated by a voltage, so I1 and V2 are the variables you can actually set, and h21 appears directly as the current gain β.

quiz.q: Which h parameters are found from a test with the output port shorted, and which from a test with the input port open?
quiz.a: Output shorted (V2 = 0) gives h11 = V1/I1 and h21 = I2/I1. Input open (I1 = 0) gives h12 = V1/V2 and h22 = I2/V2.

quiz.q: A two-port has h11 = 2 kΩ, h12 = 0, h21 = 100, h22 = 50 μS. With I1 = 20 μA and V2 = 0, find V1 and I2.
A two-port has g11 = 1 mS, g12 = 0, g21 = −2 and g22 = 500 Ω. Find h11 and h22.
A student measures h12 by shorting the output port and finds zero. What went wrong, and what does the correct test give?
quiz.a: h12 is V1/V2 with the input open (I1 = 0), not with the output shorted. With the output shorted, V2 is forced to zero and the ratio is undefined, so the reading is meaningless. The correct test opens port 1, applies V2, and measures the open-circuit voltage V1 at port 1.

beyond: Not for the exam. Transistor datasheets still print h_fe and h_ie, and circuit simulators build the hybrid-pi small-signal model from the same four ratios. At radio frequencies the open and short tests of this chapter become impossible to make cleanly, so engineers switch to S-parameters, which use matched resistive terminations instead; search "S-parameters" and "hybrid-pi model" to see the next step. The g set survives in microwave device modelling, where a voltage-driven input and a current-driven output are the convenient pair.
